items.title: Captain Verne Streckfus Interview, 1960-09-22
items.q: So we hired him. He lived up on Rampart Street at that time. And we had to go up and get him out of the room to bring him to work for you.

ctx.x: It's not interesting to me that that talk about economy at all. Where did you go to find talent?

Well, fate would go around and get the talent and he said, see, we needed a good orchestra. But this Louis Armstrong, he was touted as being so good, you know, and how would you ever get to hear him unless you went around to hear him? And I remember I went down to hear him and that night they were sitting up in the balcony. Of course, you put the room in those days. You had to get a permit to go in because it wouldn't even walk around because it was so strict. And they were all sitting up there in their shirt…
Would you go around to the night club?
